clue.text: Robber born with that certain something …

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
and means with, joining one thing to another
IT is the indefinable appeal someone has, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A thief who was born with irresistible charisma, leading on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed outlaw who robs travellers, so a robber in a broader sense.

clue.text: … something inherited in Guernsey regularly

indicators.note: regularly says to take every other letter of the word Guernsey, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Continuing from the robber, a trait passed down among the people of Guernsey, a Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Genes are the units of heredity passed from parents to offspring.

clue.text: Difference shown by prisoner getting fresh start

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: fresh suggests the word start is made anew, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A released convict making a fresh start shows a marked change from before.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrast is a striking dissimilarity between two things.

clue.text: Lettuce variety firm and small

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A greengrocer describing a type of lettuce as crisp and compact.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is the long-leaved lettuce also called romaine.

clue.text: Had race fixed — that's a ridiculous pretence

indicators.note: a fixed race is rigged, and here the words had race are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rigged horse race exposed as a farce.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is an absurd pretence meant to keep up appearances.

clue.text: Having role in South Africa's ancient city

indicators.note: in places the word for a role within the abbreviation for South Africa

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: An actor landing a role in South Africa's oldest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece, rival to Athens.

clue.text: Enticement in crude panto time after time

indicators.note: crude suggests something rough and unrefined, so the letters of panto and time are knocked about

explanation.surface: Bawdy pantomime humour that keeps tempting the audience again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time after time' supplies the word time plus its abbreviation; 'crude' scrambles panto with the word, giving EMPTATION after the lone T.
explanation.definitionFit: Temptation is the act of luring someone, an enticement.

clue.text: Spanish wine and pork pie right for royalist

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine
pork pie, or porky pie, is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

explanation.surface: A Spanish lunch of sparkling wine and a pork pie, fit for a royalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang (where a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with) for a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavaliers were the supporters of King Charles I in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Stay within budget, as Chunnel consortium had to?

definitions.meaning: the Channel Tunnel was bored from both England and France, and the two ends had to meet in the middle

explanation.surface: The firm building the Channel Tunnel had to keep its costs under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chunnel is the Channel Tunnel between England and France, dug from each side towards the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having just enough money for one's needs; literally the tunnel's two halves had to join.

clue.text: Home not yet marvellous?

parts.note: pre- as a prefix means before, so not yet
fab is slang short for fabulous, marvellous

explanation.surface: A house that is not quite wonderful yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, built quickly after the Second World War in Britain.

clue.text: Tom Sawyer maybe rude: tavern in uproar!

indicators.note: in uproar suggests chaos, so the letters of rude and tavern are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Mark Twain's boy hero being rude while a tavern erupts into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is an example of a bold seeker of adventure, as 'maybe' signals.

clue.text: Compete against Liberal cutting wages

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the letter for Liberal goes inside the word for wages

parts.note: pay means wages

explanation.surface: A political contest where the Liberal party proposes cutting wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a team is to compete against it.

clue.text: Greek deity once featured in two articles

indicators.note: featured in means appearing within, so the word for once sits between the articles

parts.note: A and A are two indefinite articles
then means once, at a former time

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess who used to appear in a pair of magazine pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom and war.

clue.text: Timber lifting in Noah's Ark

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means reading upwards, so the hidden letters are reversed
in says the letters lie inside the words Noah's Ark

explanation.surface: Wood being hoisted aboard Noah's Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood tree, and its wood is used for timber.

clue.text: Natural way to achieve financial independence?

parts.note: an easy manner is a natural, relaxed one
a street is a way, as in road names

explanation.surface: Asking for the effortless route to being financially self-sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for being comfortably off, free of money worries.

clue.text: 26 in 11, Spaniards eat more nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the words that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Spanish people eating more nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 and 11 refer to the answers CHARACTERS and PLAY, so the definition reads 'characters in play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramatis personae is the Latin heading for the list of the people in a play.

clue.text: Amply bearded king in his utility vehicle?

indicators.note: in places the letter for king within his and the utility vehicle

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
ute is short for utility vehicle, a pickup

explanation.surface: A shaggy-bearded king driving his pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy, and a full beard makes a face hairy.

clue.text: He is the lightest one!

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, the lightest of the noble gases

explanation.surface: A boast that some man weighs less than anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: He looks like a pronoun but is the symbol for helium; hydrogen is lighter but reactive, so helium is lightest of its group.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is the lightest member of the unreactive noble gas family.

clue.text: Do we hear Capone is mocking African port?

indicators.note: do we hear signals that the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster; mocking is jeering, so is mocking gives jeers

explanation.surface: Asking whether gangster Al Capone is heard ridiculing a North African harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Algiers is the capital of Algeria and a major Mediterranean seaport.

clue.text: Age concealed by fat old polymath

indicators.note: concealed by means hidden inside, so the word for age goes into the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
an eon is an age, a vast period

explanation.surface: Ageing hidden under the paunch of an elderly genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, painter, engineer and inventor, is the classic example of a polymath.

clue.text: Perkins or Lawley say to take legal action

definitions.meaning: ... Perkins and ... Lawley are British television and radio presenters

explanation.surface: A broadcaster preparing to go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Both presenters share a first name, which is also the verb for bringing a court case.

clue.text: Romeo over the moon and part of the family

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the letter for Romeo above the rest

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
over the moon is a British idiom for delighted, elated

explanation.surface: Romeo overjoyed at being accepted into Juliet's family.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone related belongs to the same family by blood or marriage.

clue.text: See 14
Sweet drink to hand when holding court

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the court abbreviation goes inside the word for to hand

parts.note: to hand means nearby, near

explanation.surface: Keeping a sweet beverage within reach during a court session.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is a sugary fluid, and by extension any delicious drink, the drink of the gods.

clue.text: O! Aren't bananas sumptuous?

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of aren't are scrambled

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising how rich and luxurious bananas are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the subject of the question but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means richly decorated, as sumptuous furnishings are.

clue.text: Sailor to attain goal

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get is to attain

explanation.surface: A seaman setting out to achieve an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is an objective one aims at.

clue.text: Hot body that ultimately squeezes into short sari

indicators.note: squeezes into means pressing inside, so the final letter of that goes within the cut-down garment
short means curtailed, so the word sari loses its final letter
ultimately points to the final letter of the word that

explanation.surface: An attractive figure squeezing into a skimpy sari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot body' sounds like a description of a person but means a celestial body that burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a glowing ball of gas in space, an astronomical body of intense heat.

clue.text: Cleaner moving crates and cases

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British term for a cleaning lady

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters of crates are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner shifting crates and packing cases around.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is an informal word for an eccentric person, as is a character.

clue.text: Boring master

definitions.meaning: to ... an animal is to master it

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means insipid, and the verb means to subdue or domesticate.

clue.text: Brownie perhaps arrived with artist

parts.note: came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A Brownie, the junior Girl Guide, turning up with a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownie suggests a young Girl Guide, but the Kodak Brownie was a popular cheap box camera.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie is an example of a simple photographic apparatus.

clue.text: See 8
Stick man?

definitions.meaning: A man's name, short for Roderick or Rodney

explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a thin straight piece of wood, and also a common male first name.
